title: Bebe Rexha & Faithless’ ‘New Religion’ Hits No. 1 on WARM Global Dance Radio Chart
summary: The chart ranks the top dance tracks worldwide, based on monitored airplay across 200-plus dance stations in more than 30 countries.
contentText:
Bebe Rexha and Faithless hit No. 1 on the WARM Global Dance Radio chart as “New Religion” rises a spot to the top of the ranking dated May 23.

Released in early March, the track leads with 900-plus spins across more than 200 monitored stations worldwide in the May 8-14 tracking week, according to World Airplay Radio Monitor.

The song has also found success across Billboard ’s U.S.-based charts, spending a week at No. 1 on the Dance/Mix Show Airplay chart (dated May 9) and reaching No. 29 on Pop Airplay and No. 33 on Rhythmic Airplay.

“New Religion” interpolates Faithless’ 1995 song “Insomnia,” which was a Billboard hit in its own right. The track spent a week at No. 1 on the Dance Club Songs chart in 1997 and reached No. 62 on the Billboard Hot 100 . A reworked version, “Insomnia 2.0,” spent a week at No. 1 on Dance Club Songs in 2015.

“New Religion” marks the first WARM Global Dance Radio No. 1 for both Rexha and Faithless since Billboard began publishing the chart in March.

Elsewhere in the chart’s top five, ANOTR’s “Talk to You,” featuring 54 Ultra, falls to No. 2 after spending six weeks at No. 1; FISHER and Tones and I’s “Favour” holds at its No. 3 high; Prospa and Cloonee’s “Free Your Mind” rises 5-4, returning to its peak; and Milky and Mall Grab’s “Just the Way You Are” rises 7-5 after reaching No. 2 in April.

Calvin Harris and Jazzy’s “Satisfy” is the top debut on this week’s chart, at No. 14. Harris spent four weeks at No. 1 on the ranking in March-April with “Release the Pressure,” alongside Kasabian.

Dom Dolla and Tiga’s “Don’t Worry Baby” also debuts in the top 20, at No. 16.

As announced March 5, Billboard has expanded its dance chart portfolio with the inclusion of the WARM Global Dance Radio chart. The ranking debuted on Billboard.com March 10, joining Billboard ’s long-standing U.S.-based dance lists, including Hot Dance/Electronic Songs, Hot Dance/Pop Songs, Dance/Mix Show Airplay and Top Dance Albums. The 40-position Global Dance Radio chart (published in full as a 100-position ranking on WARM’s platform) aggregates plays from 200-plus dance-dedicated radio stations across more than 30 countries, reflecting songs trending globally through a network of programmers and radio gatekeepers operating across multiple territories.

Check out the top 40 of the WARM Global Dance Radio chart on Billboard.com and head over to WARM’s website for the full 100-position survey.
